answer: Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. Fingerprints are counted in ferrous, which means the distribution is public, and jade lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a mirror header, so 4038 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 34 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
